''macrophylla''''' is a [[subspecies]] of ''[[Boehmeria virgata]]'', a [[flowering plant]] in the nettle [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Urticaceae. This [[herbaceous plant]] [[perennial]] is native to tropical Africa and the western Indian Ocean.{{Cite POWO|title=''Boehmeria virgata'' subsp. ''macrophylla'' (Hornem.) Friis & Wilmot-Dear|id=77133790-1|access-date=2024-01-13|mode=cs1}} Some sources say that it is also native to China. The flowers are [[Dioecy|dioecious]] or [[Monoecy|monoecious]]. Its flowering season is from June to September. It is commonly found in forests, thickets, along streams and roadsides. It is characterized by the opposite leaves, spike-like [[inflorescence]]s, and fruiting [[perianth]]s with a rounded base.{{cite web|title=''Boehmeria macrophylla'' Hornemann, Hort. Bot. Hafn. 2: 890. 1815.|url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200006391|website=Flora of China|date=16 January 2015}} ==Uses== The fibre of the stem is shiny, white and strong, and is used for making sacks, bags, rough clothes, nets, and rope. It is possibly useful for textiles. The woody parts are moderately hard but too small for woodworking; however they make a good fuel.{{cite web|title=Boehmeria macrophylla - Hornem.|url=http://www.pfaf.org/user/Plant.aspx?LatinName=Boehmeria+macrophylla|website=www.pfaf.org|accessdate=16 January 2015}}
''Boehmeria virgata'' subsp. ''macrophylla'' has some applications in [[traditional medicine]], including as a tonic, for treating boils and for [[dermatitis]]. It is also used as an insecticide.{{cite journal|last1=Rahmatullah|first1=Muhammed|title=A Survey of Medicinal Plants Used by Kavirajes of Chalna Area, Khulna District, Bangladesh|journal=African Journal of Traditional, Complementary and Alternative Medicines|date=2010|volume=7|issue=2|pages=91–97|doi=10.4314/ajtcam.v7i2.50859 |pmid=21304618 |pmc=3021158 }} ==References== {{Reflist}} {{Taxonbar|from1=Q124260756|from2=Q91558277|from3=Q11130490}} [[Category:Boehmeria|virgata macrophylla]] {{Urticaceae-stub}}
